Observer pattern:
- Behavioral design pattern, subject maintains list observers, notifies on state changes.

B-trees:
- Self-balancing tree, nodes with multiple keys/children, sorted, optimized for disk/block storage. Generalization of BST; all leaves same depth; internal nodes have between ceil(m/2) and m children; root exceptions.
- How works: search from root, compare keys, descend; insert: search leaf, insert key, split if overflow, promote median; delete: borrow/merge, rebalance.
- Time complexity: O(log_m n) comparisons? Actually height O(log_m n), but within node binary/linear search O(log m) or O(m). For disk, m large, height small. Space O(n). B-trees minimize disk I/O: height ~ log_m n, each node fits block.
- Alternatives: AVL/red-black trees (in-memory, O(log n), lower constants? B-trees also used in memory due cache), skip lists, hash tables (not ordered), sorted arrays. Choose B-tree for large datasets, disk/SSD, range queries, databases, filesystems. AVL/RB for in-memory ordered maps with frequent updates. Hash for exact lookup no order.
